routes.reason: New roadmap SpringerResolutionAndCharacteristicCycles, 29 items. Accepted. The reason does not merely assert novelty: it records that no atlas stage mentions the Springer or Grothendieck simultaneous resolution, the Steinberg variety or the nilpotent cone, and it names the near neighbours and says how each differs — ET.2 owns perverse sheaves and Hitchin geometry, GeometricSatakeAndFusion owns the Fargues–Fontaine curve. I confirmed the name is free and proposed by no other paper. The brief states what is to be built precisely (g̃ as a vector bundle over G/B, Grothendieck's simultaneous resolution with its properness and étale degree |W| over the regular semisimple locus, X = g̃ ×_g g̃ and the vector bundle V_w → U_w) and imports the Tau Ceti Borel–Weil and Bruhat material rather than rebuilding it. That import is real: the paper's §2 rests on it, and this review verified that the two planned items pointing at the Tau Ceti LieGroups and LieHighestWeight layers resolve.

New roadmap TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel, 67 items and the largest route. Accepted, and the reason is the most carefully evidenced of the seven: it records that the word 'trianguline' occurs in the atlas only as an adjective inside hypotheses of CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility and in a GL₂(Q_p) block check, never as the geometric object X_tri(r̄). So the object itself is unowned, while its ambient space and coefficients do have owners — which routes 5 and 7 import rather than duplicate. That division is exactly right: the trianguline variety is a closed subvariety of 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_L, and 𝔛_r̄ is sent to LocalGaloisDeformationRings. The brief states the construction in order, from almost de Rham B_dR-representations and Fontaine's equivalence through the deformation groupoids to the identification with completions of g and g̃. The name is free; three other papers propose it identically, which is a merge and not a conflict.

Part II of CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility, 27 items. Accepted on the mathematics: the reason identifies precisely what the parent already owns (R31.1 towers and completed cohomology, R31.2 classical specialisations and locally algebraic vectors, R31.3 Hecke and deformation actions, R31.5 patched completed modules and support) and what it does not — its stages are written for modular and Shimura curves, that is GL₂ over Q, and none plans an eigenvariety for a definite unitary group or the patched eigenvariety. The brief says so in its first sentence. ONE POINT REFERRED UPWARD RATHER THAN EDITED: the title is 'Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility, Part II: …', while the parent's title is 'Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility OVER Q'. Dropping 'over Q' means the title is not literally the '<base roadmap>, Part II: …' form PROTOCOL 15 prescribes — and the omission may well be deliberate, since this paper works over a CM field and not over Q. I did not change it, because PAPER-DING-25 and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 propose this roadmap with byte-identical id, parent and title, and editing one of three would break the merge. The maintainer should decide whether all three gain 'over Q' or whether the parent's title is read with 'over Q' as a scope note.

Source addition to PadicHodgeTheory:P7, 3 items. P7 owns the Robba foundations and the representation-theoretic handoffs, which is where §3.1's B_dR-representations, the almost de Rham condition, Fontaine's equivalence W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) and Berger's W⁺_dR and W_dR belong. The reason is right that this paper is specifically a source for the almost de Rham part, which is the form of Fontaine's theory the whole local model runs on — and that is also the object of finding E7, where the paper itself slips and writes D_dR for D_pdR.

Source additions to LocalGaloisDeformationRings at R08.1 and R08.3, 2 items. R08.1 owns unrestricted framed local deformation rings and R08.3 potentially semistable deformation spaces, which is exactly what §3.6's framed deformation groupoids and §3.7's ambient space 𝔛_r̄ are. The reason draws the boundary explicitly — the trianguline variety itself goes to route 2, its ambient space is imported from here — which is the right way to keep the new roadmap from absorbing material that already has an owner.

Source additions to CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility at R31.2 and R31.5, 2 items. The completed cohomology and patched representation of §5.1 are the definite-unitary-group analogues of what those stages plan for modular and Shimura curves, so they are sources; the genuinely new material goes to route 3. The split between this route and route 3 is drawn along the same line the parent's own stages draw, which is what makes both defensible.

Source additions to PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology at PG.3 and PG.7, 3 items. The reason quotes PG.7's own description — 'the affinoid/relative Robba category of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao', with the relative Herr and Iwasawa complexes, their finiteness and base change — and notes that data/restructure/RS-26 keeps triangulation and exceptional loci in that stage. PG.3 owns the Herr three-term complex, which is the (φ,γ_K)-cohomology used here. Quoting the target stage rather than paraphrasing it is the right standard for a source route.

notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5. Verdict accept, and nothing needed correcting in place — the first extraction in this reviewer's run of which that is true. All 135 items, 7 routes and 11 recorded mistakes were checked against the published Numdam text, re-fetched and hashing to 34ffd697…3967a, matching the record; printed page = PDF page + 298, as the source block states. All 11 mistakes are confirmed. Several are settled by the paper contradicting itself, which is the strongest kind of evidence available for a misprint: E2, where the 'equivalently' clause on p. 352 uses 'and' where the definition one sentence earlier forces 'or … for some i ≠ j' — and since ε is not algebraic, the printed condition is unsatisfiable, making T₀ⁿ = T_Lⁿ and collapsing the genericity locus on which §§3–4 run; E4, where Lemma 5.2.4 on p. 393 repeats the first assertion of Lemma 5.2.3 word for word and so is empty as printed, while its own proof dévisses from Verma modules and proves the statement for an arbitrary object of category O; E5, where 2.2.1 is a Proposition on p. 311 and cited as such on pp. 315 and 320 but as a Lemma on p. 313; and E6, where one clause on p. 323 writes P_{w,w′} without w₀ and P_{w₀w,w₀w} with it, against the convention stated on p. 321. E3 was checked on a page image, because its relation symbol and its (in)equality are each a single glyph the text layer drops. The extraction's quotation is exactly right — '≠ 0 if w_R ≼ w', which distinguishes the Claim from the vanishing statement (5.15) higher on the same page — and so is its correction: y is a general point of the patched space whose Weyl element was introduced two paragraphs earlier as w_y 'as we defined w_R in (5.13)', and Step 4 immediately below reads 'such that w_y ≼ w'. For E7 through E11 each finding bundles a principal element with one or two subsidiary ones. The principal element of each is confirmed against the published text; where a subsidiary element rests on the extraction's reading rather than on a check of mine, the verdict says so explicitly. All 12 planned items name atlas layers that exist, all 123 missing items are routed exactly once, and the extraction records no library items, which is right: nothing in this paper is in the pinned libraries. There is no run-together numbering anywhere in the file. The routes are the best-evidenced this reviewer has seen: route 2 establishes that 'trianguline' appears in the atlas only as an adjective and never as the geometric object X_tri(r̄); route 1 names its near neighbours and says how each differs; route 7 quotes its target stage's own description. Both new roadmap names are free, and three other papers — PAPER-DING-25, PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 and PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 — propose them with byte-identical id, parent and title, so these are merges rather than conflicts. ONE POINT IS REFERRED TO THE MAINTAINER RATHER THAN EDITED. The Part II title drops 'over Q' from its parent's title ('Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility over Q'), so it is not literally the '<base>, Part II: …' form PROTOCOL 15 prescribes. The omission may be deliberate, since this paper works over a CM field. It is shared verbatim with the two co-proposing papers, so correcting it here alone would desynchronise the three proposals and break the merge that their agreement makes possible. The decision belongs to whoever merges them. Every check is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19.md.
